courseTitle: The Romans in Britain — Invasion & Legacy (55 BC–AD 410)
disclaimer: The History Revision Hub — Key Stage 2 Primary History Mind Map.

root.label: The Romans in Britain
root.gloss: How Claudius’s Roman legions conquered Celtic Britain in AD 43, defeated Boudicca, built Hadrian’s Wall, straight roads, and steam baths, and left a lasting legacy after AD 410.

children.label: 1. Celts & AD 43 Invasion
children.gloss: Skilled Iron Age Celtic tribes farmed roundhouses and traded metals across the Channel before Emperor Claudius invaded with 40,000 legionaries and war elephants in AD 43.

children.label: 1. Celtic Britain Before Rome
children.q2Chain: Separate Celtic tribes & Maiden Castle → Smoky thatched roundhouses → Gold torcs & Cornish tin draw Rome’s eye
children.gloss: Separate Celtic tribes & Maiden Castle → Smoky thatched roundhouses → Gold torcs & Cornish tin draw Rome’s eye

children.label: Tribes, Hillforts & Caesar
children.gloss: Separate tribes like the Iceni, Catuvellauni, and Brigantes guarded earth hillforts and fought off Julius Caesar in 55–54 BC.

children.label: Iceni, Catuvellauni & Brigantes
children.gloss: Zero single king ruled Britain; Separate tribes guarded own lands.

children.label: Maiden Castle & Caesar Repelled
children.gloss: Steep earth ramparts ringed hilltops; Chariots fought Caesar 55–54 BC.

children.label: → Sheltered Busy Roundhouse Farms
children.gloss: Protected tribal cattle behind ditches; Kept Britain free another century.

children.label: Smoky Thatched Roundhouses
children.gloss: Celtic families wove wattle-and-daub walls under chimney-free thatched roofs, curing meat in smoke and grinding wheat on quern stones.

children.label: No Chimney Stopped Roof Sparks
children.gloss: Plastered hazel sticks with clay; Wind could not fan flames.

children.label: Hearth Smoke, Looms & Querns
children.gloss: Woodsmoke cured meat, chased bugs; Wove bright wool; ground flour.

children.label: → Fed Skilled Smiths & Traders
children.gloss: Warm central hearth heated families; Supported thriving craft workshops.

children.label: Gold Torcs, Druids & Tin Trade
children.gloss: Celtic smiths twisted gold torcs, Druids memorised laws orally, and ships traded Cornish tin and wheat across the Channel.

children.label: Twisted Gold Torcs & Druids
children.gloss: Placed bronze shields in rivers; Druids memorised laws without books.

children.label: Cornish Tin & Gold Stater Coins
children.gloss: Exported tin, iron, hides, wheat; Minted galloping gold stater coins.

children.label: → Tempted Claudius to Invade Next
children.gloss: Spread news of British riches; Caught ambitious Rome’s attention.

children.label: 2. Claudius Invades (AD 43)
children.q2Chain: Claudius seeks military glory & tin/silver → Legionaries lock testudo tortoise shields → War elephants capture Colchester
children.gloss: Claudius seeks military glory & tin/silver → Legionaries lock testudo tortoise shields → War elephants capture Colchester

children.label: Claudius Craves Glory & Metals
children.gloss: Doubted by senators for his limp and stutter, Emperor Claudius invaded in AD 43 for glory, silver, tin, wheat, and taxes.

children.label: Senators Doubted Nervous Claudius
children.gloss: Walked with limp and stutter; Needed quick famous military glory.

children.label: Silver, Tin, Wheat & Taxes
children.gloss: Rich silver, tin, lead, iron; Southern wheat and new taxes.

children.label: → Launched 40,000-Strong Fleet
children.gloss: Gathered four full-time Roman legions; Sailed across Channel in AD 43.

children.label: Tortoise Shields & Short Swords
children.gloss: Full-time legionaries marched 20 miles a day in strip armour, locked scutum shields into a testudo, and fought with pilum and gladius.

children.label: Iron Strip Armour & Testudo
children.gloss: Marched 20 miles in caligae; Locked scutum shields like tortoise.

children.label: Bending Pilum & Short Gladius
children.gloss: Pilum javelin ruined enemy shields; Stabbed close with gladius sword.

children.label: → Outmatched Part-Time Warriors
children.gloss: Trained daily as calm team; Pushed inland from Kent coast.

children.label: Medway Battle & War Elephants
children.gloss: Aulus Plautius landed at Richborough and beat Caratacus at the Medway before Claudius entered Camulodunum with war elephants.

children.label: Richborough & Two-Day Medway
children.gloss: 40,000 landed at Kent Richborough; Defeated Caratacus at River Medway.

children.label: Elephants Captured Camulodunum
children.gloss: War elephants terrified Celtic horses; Eleven British kings surrendered.

children.label: → Harsh Rule Sparked AD 60 Revolt
children.gloss: Turned south into Roman province; Greedy taxes angered British tribes.

children.label: 2. Boudicca & Hadrian’s Wall
children.gloss: Broken Roman promises sparked Queen Boudicca’s fiery AD 60–61 rebellion before Emperor Hadrian built a 73-mile stone frontier guarded by troops from three continents.

children.label: 3. Boudicca’s Revolt (AD 60–61)
children.q2Chain: Rome betrays King Prasutagus’s will (AD 60) → Boudicca burns three Roman towns to red clay → Narrow valley defeat at Watling Street
children.gloss: Rome betrays King Prasutagus’s will (AD 60) → Boudicca burns three Roman towns to red clay → Narrow valley defeat at Watling Street

children.label: Broken Promises to the Iceni
children.gloss: When Iceni ally King Prasutagus left half his wealth to Emperor Nero, greedy officials seized lands and flogged Queen Boudicca.

children.label: Prasutagus’s Will Broken in AD 60
children.gloss: Left half wealth to Nero; Soldiers seized East Anglian lands.

children.label: Loans Demanded & Boudicca Flogged
children.gloss: Demanded heavy Roman loans back; Cruelly mistreated her two daughters.

children.label: → United Iceni & Trinovantes
children.gloss: Boudicca rode wooden war chariot; Marched while Paulinus fought Anglesey.

children.label: Three Towns Burn to Red Clay
children.gloss: While Governor Suetonius Paulinus was in Anglesey, rebels torched Camulodunum, Londinium, and Verulamium into red clay.

children.label: Colchester, London & St Albans
children.gloss: Burned Camulodunum’s hated Roman temple; Torched busy Londinium and Verulamium.

children.label: Buried Red Clay Destruction Layer
children.gloss: Burning shops baked red clay; Diggers find melted pots, coins.

children.label: → Forced Paulinus Down Watling St
children.gloss: Paulinus raced south from Wales; Chose narrow valley for showdown.

children.label: Showdown on Watling Street
children.gloss: In AD 61, 10,000 disciplined legionaries in a narrow wooded valley pinned squashed Britons back against their own wooden wagons.

children.label: Narrow Valley Guarded Roman Sides
children.gloss: 10,000 legionaries stood outnumbered; Iceni parked ring of wagons.

children.label: Tight Wedges Pinned Rebel Crowd
children.gloss: Squashed Britons could barely swing; Hurled javelins; trapped against wagons.

children.label: Secured South Behind Stone Walls
children.gloss: Boudicca died soon after battle; Londinium rebuilt inside stone walls.

children.label: 4. Hadrian’s Wall & Vindolanda
children.q2Chain: Emperor Hadrian builds 73-mile stone wall (AD 122) → Oxygen-free mud saves Vindolanda letters → Troops from three continents guard frontier
children.gloss: Emperor Hadrian builds 73-mile stone wall (AD 122) → Oxygen-free mud saves Vindolanda letters → Troops from three continents guard frontier

children.label: 73 Miles of Stone Sea to Sea
children.gloss: Visiting in AD 122, Emperor Hadrian ordered a 73-mile stone wall with milecastles and 16 forts like Housesteads.

children.label: Stop Raids & Tax Border Trade
children.gloss: Divided province from northern Caledonia; Ran Wallsend to Bowness-on-Solway.

children.label: Milecastles & 16 Stone Forts
children.gloss: Gatehouse built every Roman mile; Rainwater flushed stone fort latrines.

children.label: → Settled Busy Frontier Garrisons
children.gloss: 80 Roman miles across north; Soldiers wrote letters nearby.

children.label: Vindolanda Wooden Ink Letters
children.gloss: Wet oxygen-free mud at Vindolanda Fort preserved wooden ink tablets including a birthday party invite and parcel of socks.

children.label: Wet Airless Mud Stopped Rotting
children.gloss: Buried beneath Vindolanda Fort floors; Saved hundreds of wooden tablets.

children.label: Birthday Invite & Woollen Socks
children.gloss: Claudia Severa’s 11 September party; Sent socks, sandals, two underpants.

children.label: Oldest Woman’s Latin Handwriting
children.gloss: Invited friend Sulpicia Lepidina warmly; Proved chilly real frontier life.

children.label: Troops From Three Continents
children.gloss: Auxiliaries from Europe, Syria, and North Africa patrolled the Wall while families lived in vici towns like Arbeia.

children.label: Batavians, Syrians & North Africans
children.gloss: Aurelian Moors at Burgh-by-Sands; Guarded windy northern border.

children.label: Vici Towns: Barates, Regina, Victor
children.gloss: Syrian Barates wed British Regina; Tombstone honoured Mauretanian Victor.

children.label: Multi-Continental Roman Britain
children.gloss: Shopkeepers bustled outside Arbeia gates; Linked Europe, Syria, North Africa.

children.label: 3. Towns, AD 410 & Legacy
children.gloss: Rome built 10,000 miles of straight stone highways, steam baths, and mosaic villas before legions left in AD 410, leaving roads, towns, letters, and calendar months.

children.label: 5. Roads, Baths & Villas
children.q2Chain: 10,000 miles of groma-sighted roads & forums → Aqueducts & hypocaust baths at Aquae Sulis → Mosaic villas vs 9-in-10 rural roundhouses
children.gloss: 10,000 miles of groma-sighted roads & forums → Aqueducts & hypocaust baths at Aquae Sulis → Mosaic villas vs 9-in-10 rural roundhouses

children.label: 10,000 Miles of Straight Roads
children.gloss: Using a wooden groma, surveyors laid 10,000 miles of cambered stone roads linking walled forum towns and Caerleon’s amphitheatre.

children.label: Groma Sighting & Cambered Stone
children.gloss: Curved stones drained rain into ditches; Carts rolled fast all year.

children.label: Curved stones drained rain into ditches
children.gloss: Curved stones drained rain into ditches

children.label: Forums, Basilicas & Amphitheatres
children.gloss: Grid towns centred on forums; Gladiator crowds cheered at Caerleon.

children.label: → Created First Stone Urban Hubs
children.gloss: Replaced slow muddy dirt tracks; Brought fresh water into towns.

children.label: Aqueducts & Hypocaust Baths
children.gloss: Aqueducts and lead pipes fed Aquae Sulis bathhouses heated underneath by furnace-fed hypocaust brick stacks.

children.label: Aqueducts, Pipes & Aquae Sulis
children.gloss: Fresh spring water fed fountains; Townsfolk chatted daily at Bath.

children.label: Hypocaust Heat & Bronze Strigils
children.gloss: Hot air blew between pilae; Scraped olive oil with strigils.

children.label: → Luxury for Rich Town Elites
children.gloss: Enslaved workers stoked wood furnaces; Inspired grand southern country villas.

children.label: Mosaics vs 9-in-10 Roundhouses
children.gloss: Rich elites laid mosaic floors at Fishbourne Palace, yet nearly nine in ten Britons kept farming in thatched roundhouses.

children.label: Fishbourne Mosaics & Garum Sauce
children.gloss: Pressed tiny coloured tesserae cubes; Tasted cherries, walnuts, salty garum.

children.label: Nine in Ten Kept Roundhouses
children.gloss: Spoke Celtic across rural farms; Still paid heavy Roman taxes.

children.label: Rich Villas Beside Deep Continuity
children.gloss: Towns changed far more than farms; Until coastal raiders struck c. 400.

children.label: Towns changed far more than farms
children.gloss: Towns changed far more than farms

children.label: 6. Leaving AD 410 & Legacy
children.q2Chain: Raiders strike & Honorius’s AD 410 reply → Bathhouses crumble & Hoxne silver buried → Roads, -chester towns, ABCs & calendar live on
children.gloss: Raiders strike & Honorius’s AD 410 reply → Bathhouses crumble & Hoxne silver buried → Roads, -chester towns, ABCs & calendar live on

children.label: Raiders & Honorius’s AD 410 Note
children.gloss: As Picts, Scotti, Angles, and Saxons raided coasts and Visigoths threatened Rome, Emperor Honorius told Britain to defend itself in AD 410.

children.label: Coasts Raided & Rome Attacked
children.gloss: Picts, Scotti, Angles, Saxons raided; Visigoths invaded Italy toward Rome.

children.label: AD 410: Defend Yourselves Alone
children.gloss: Legions sailed back across Channel; Honorius had zero spare soldiers.

children.label: → Ended 400 Years of Army Rule
children.gloss: Fresh wage coins stopped arriving; Town markets and potteries shrank.

children.label: Crumbling Baths & Silver Hoards
children.gloss: As aqueducts and bathhouses crumbled, anxious rich families buried silver chests like the Hoxne Hoard and Mildenhall Treasure.

children.label: Coins Stopped & Baths Crumbled
children.gloss: Nobody fixed leaky stone aqueducts; Fearing raiders along open coasts.

children.label: Hoxne & Mildenhall Silver Buried
children.gloss: Hid gold coins, silver spoons; Suffolk farmers ploughed them up.

children.label: Saved Glittering Time Capsules
children.gloss: Many owners never came home; Revealed final Romano-British wealth.

children.label: Roman Clues Around Us Today
children.gloss: London, straight A-roads, -chester fort names, Latin ABCs, Roman numerals, July and August, and apples still shape Britain.

children.label: London, A-Roads & -Chester Towns
children.gloss: Londinium grew into modern London; -chester marks Roman castra forts.

children.label: Latin ABCs, Clocks & Calendar
children.gloss: ABC letters and I, V, X; July, August, Christianity, sweet apples.

children.label: ABC letters and I, V, X
children.gloss: ABC letters and I, V, X

children.label: Shaped Everyday British Life
children.gloss: Brought cabbages, rabbits, and nettles; Set stage for Anglo-Saxon settlers.
